Which activity best develops the concept of area in Class VI before the formula is introduced?
options: Telling learners to memorise length x breadth
Covering shapes with unit square tiles or counting squares on grid paper
Asking learners to copy formulas from the board
Giving a test on area formulas
questions.exp: Counting unit squares builds meaning of area; formulas then emerge from patterns.

questions.q: Find the next pair: AZ, BY, CX, DW, ?
questions.exp: The first letter moves forward and the second moves backward by one each time: D→E and W→V, giving EV.

questions.q: Find the missing number: 5, 6, 8, 11, 15, 20, ?
questions.exp: The differences are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, so the next difference is 6: 20 + 6 = 26.

questions.q: Find the odd letter group.
questions.exp: In CEG, KMO and QSU the letters are two places apart each time; in TVY the gaps are 2 and 3.

questions.q:
Statements: All engineers are graduates. All graduates are citizens. Some citizens are artists.
Conclusions: I. All engineers are citizens. II. Some artists are graduates.
questions.exp: I follows from the chain engineer → graduate → citizen. The artists among the citizens may not be graduates, so II does not follow.

questions.q: How many times do the hands of a clock form a right angle in 12 hours?
questions.exp: The hands are at right angles 2 times in each hour on average (the relative gain of 5.5° per minute gives 90° and 270° once each per 12/11 hours), so 22 times in 12 hours.
